events.description: It is a dark and stormy night and veteran detective Jack Russell is murdered at his own retirement party. events.description: In this work, I am weaving text from performance scores and personal poetry to create a solo performance entitled BAD CLAY, an experience that experiments with the intersection of Ceramics and Performance. Driving the work are questions around migration and immigration (where do bodies come from and what are they destined for?), intimacy (how can bodies connect through clay?), and performance art (what are all of the expressions of clay and performance that already exist and how can we further their possibilities?). events.title: Kramer / Fauci
events.venue: FringeArts, 140 N Christopher Columbus Blvd, Philadelphia, PA 19106
events.description:
“God, I hated him.” —Larry Kramer on Anthony Fauci, 2002
“It turned out I loved the guy, and I think he loved me back.” —Anthony Fauci on Larry Kramer, 2020
Internationally acclaimed director Daniel Fish (Oklahoma!) turns his eye to one of the most combustible conversations of the AIDS crisis: the 1993 televised clash between Dr. Anthony Fauci, the nation’s leading AIDS researcher, and playwright-activist Larry Kramer. A confrontation charged with rage, urgency, and unexpected intimacy, it crystallized a turning point in the fight for care, treatment, and recognition. Fish dramatizes their exchange as both history and provocation, a searing reminder of how art, activism, and public health collide on the most human terms.

Ink & Melanin: Verse One is a poetic narrative documentary that centers the beauty, strength, and complexity of dark-skinned Black women. Through original poetry, evocative imagery, and intimate soundbites, the film weaves together a meditation on melanin, identity, and self-definition — celebrating what has too often been diminished or overlooked.
At its heart, Ink & Melanin: Verse One is a love letter — to dark-skinned Black women, and to anyone who has ever had to reclaim their own beauty on their own terms. Tender, celebratory, meditative, and defiant, the film moves through a full emotional landscape, refusing to reduce its subjects to a single story.

Wherever You Are is a site-specific immersive sound experience composed and guided by Joshua Marquez. Audiences will never share the same experience and will have to navigate the Pocket Park to weave their own sonic tapestry, composing their own piece based on where they sit, stand, or situate.

events.description: On Puerto Rican Independence Day, former elected governor Cesar tells her daughter, Valentina, the story of how his relationship with Valentina’s mother, Alba, shaped the political future of Puerto Rico 16 years ago. Some emotions never become words. They stay in the body, returning with the wind, the tide and the fading light. She Carries the Moon is a dance film shaped by movement, silence and atmosphere, following a woman through solitude, memory and the search for her own voice.

Filmed on the shoreline, where the sea is constantly changing yet always returning, the work reflects on how memory lives in the body and how we continue to carry experiences long after they have passed.

events.description: Bartram’s Garden is the oldest surviving botanical garden in North America. Located in an urban neighborhood, it is a gem of nature that may seem incongruous to first-time visitors. In the 1720s, botanist John Bartram built a stone house overlooking the Schuylkill River, and began farming the 107 acres of land around it. In his spare time, Bartram followed his interest in native plant species and traveled widely collecting plants and seeds from th northern shores of Nova Scotia to the southern tip of Florida. events.title: Kramer / Fauci
events.venue: FringeArts, 140 N Christopher Columbus Blvd, Philadelphia, PA 19106
events.description:
“God, I hated him.” —Larry Kramer on Anthony Fauci, 2002
“It turned out I loved the guy, and I think he loved me back.” —Anthony Fauci on Larry Kramer, 2020
Internationally acclaimed director Daniel Fish (Oklahoma!) turns his eye to one of the most combustible conversations of the AIDS crisis: the 1993 televised clash between Dr. Anthony Fauci, the nation’s leading AIDS researcher, and playwright-activist Larry Kramer. A confrontation charged with rage, urgency, and unexpected intimacy, it crystallized a turning point in the fight for care, treatment, and recognition. Fish dramatizes their exchange as both history and provocation, a searing reminder of how art, activism, and public health collide on the most human terms.
Kramer/Fauci is base

events.description:
A cozy author reading curdles into ritual. Three stories invite the audience to listen and wonder what has been listening back. My Friend, Ithamar is an intimate horror about grief, attention, and the terrible relief of being understood. Stay for the signing.
My Friend, Ithamar is a companion piece to The Watcher Sleeps (Cannonball 2025). The lights are up. The book is open. The author is charming. The audience has taken its seats. Everything looks safe because it knows exactly how safe is supposed to look.

events.title: Bartram’s Garden Photo Exhibit at Studio 34
events.venue: Studio 34, 4522 Baltimore Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19143
events.description: Bartram’s Garden is the oldest surviving botanical garden in North America. Located in an urban neighborhood, it is a gem of nature that may seem incongruous to first-time visitors. In the 1720s, botanist John Bartram built a stone house overlooking the Schuylkill River, and began farming the 107 acres of land around it. In his spare time, Bartram followed his interest in native plant species and traveled widely collecting plants and seeds from th northern shores of Nova Scotia to the southern tip of Florida. He founded a botanical garden on the five acre plot between his house and the river and developed a nursery that sold native plants and served as a base for correspondence with other botanists on both sides of the Atlantic. events.venue: Icebox Project Space Gallery
events.description:
Fire Portal is a multi-media installation and performance that uses fire both as a destructive symbol and as a means of manifestation. Through dynamic performance, imagery, sound, movement and of course, projected flame, Red Rae grapples with the idea of burning down our current systems of power to collectively imagine what might rise out of the ashes. There are so many systems of power (late stage corporate capitalism, transphobia, white supremacy and patriarchy to name a few) that many people would like to see destroyed. Fire Portal will draw on extensive research into fire as a tool of both resistance and regeneration to create an audience experience that feels both like being torn to pieces and built back up again.

events.title: Kramer / Fauci
events.venue: FringeArts, 140 N Christopher Columbus Blvd, Philadelphia, PA 19106
events.description:
“God, I hated him.” —Larry Kramer on Anthony Fauci, 2002
“It turned out I loved the guy, and I think he loved me back.” —Anthony Fauci on Larry Kramer, 2020
Internationally acclaimed director Daniel Fish (Oklahoma!) turns his eye to one of the most combustible conversations of the AIDS crisis: the 1993 televised clash between Dr. Anthony Fauci, the nation’s leading AIDS researcher, and playwright-activist Larry Kramer. A confrontation charged with rage, urgency, and unexpected intimacy, it crystallized a turning point in the fight for care, treatment, and recognition. Fish dramatizes their exchange as both history and provocation, a searing reminder of how art, activism, and public health collide on the most human terms.

events.title: Dolls
events.venue: Franklin Inn Club
events.description:
Step inside the Doll’s House, we’ve been expecting you. The Franklin Inn Club is transformed into a living playroom, where our peculiar Nora holds court. In this bold re-envisioning of Ibsen’s classic, the audience is transported into the imagination of an 11-year-old girl who acts out her life with you, her dolls. Can she break free of her world of toys, or will she forever be stuck as a plaything for others? Inspired by EgoPo's 2013 Fringe hit created by Brenna Geffers, starring Emmeline and Lane Savadove.
“Lots of girls hold a doll and make up stories, but only [this actress] holds her dolls while enacting Ibsen’s classic play” - WHYY

events.description:
There's a play happening. Right now. It's a one person show about a woman who travels to Ireland and gets haunted by a Bog Man. It's not very good.
There's another play happening. Right now. Inside the head of the actress playing the woman who travels to Ireland and gets haunted by a Bog Man.
She’s worried. She’s worried that the play is so bad that the spirit of the Bog Man has begun to haunt her. She’s worried about not finishing the play. She’s worried about finishing the play. Just what is in that room beyond the laboratory? And just why do Mother and Father have a laboratory anyway?

events.venue: The Latvian Society of Philadelphia
events.description:
Revisit the curiosity, mischief, and confusion of childhood in this drag cabaret based on themes of queer escapism found in Peter Pan. Performance artists Dicky Dutton and Heather Jones explore the gender binary of mother versus pirate and the conflicts that arise if anyone should try to outgrow those extremes. Hook and Wendy must sever from their assigned identities in order to free themselves from this haunted fairy tale, but as it turns out, they need each other to be truly liberated. They try on many literal and metaphorical hats to find the path: Pirate and mother? It’s a no go. Pirate and pirate? Maybe? Pirate and fairy? Let’s go. Bring your costume box, your outside voice, and we’ll see you on the island of Never Land.

events.title: The Holy Fool
events.venue: The Gym at Impact Services
events.description:
This world premiere dance-theater piece uses cinematic style to explore familial bonds, love, and heartache.
Mother makes dinner. Daughter sets the table. One empty chair. A knock at the door. Expecting someone? Back to dinner. You made a mistake. Everyone’s watching. The bills pile up. The job’s never done. Another disaster. And your face—it’s older. The cameras are rolling. The Fool is laughing. You’re doing just fine.
Through the eyes of an American family, The Holy Fool examines the toll of aging, grieving, and growing up in a culture where normativity is the most valuable currency. A thrilling ghost story unfolds in a dreamlike visual landscape scored by a hypnotic blend of trumpet, percussion and synthesizers. Co-Directed by Ninth Plan

events.description:

events.title: Waiting for Westy
events.venue: Yellow Bicycle Theater
events.description:
The night before their memorial is unveiled, Vietnam veterans from South Philly learn that retired General Westmoreland plans to visit their post. The third play in a trilogy about war and its aftermath that began with Ashes, Ashes (shortlisted for The Bridge Award, premiered at the 2023 Philly Fringe Festival) and continued with A Marine Walks Up to the Pearly Gates (winner of the Lieutenant William Broyles Award, preimered at the 2025 Philly Fringe Festival), Waiting for Westy follows three Vietnam veterans as they struggle to reconcile their feelings about the war and its leaders.
A new play by Joshua Crone, featuring Thoeger Hansen, Richard Roddy, Joshua Crone, Lenny Ramos, and Bob Bowersox. Assistant directed by Giacomo Badalamenti II.

events.description: AFRO is a solo juggling show that pays homage to the past, critiques the present, and speaks of a brighter, more optimistic future for Black people in the United States. This show explores some of the challenges and struggles that many of them faced in order to gain access to jobs in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics). Not only is AFRO a tribute to Black culture, but it's also an adventure through time and space accompanied with a bunch of fun and interesting contemporary juggling tricks!

We have been hosting monthly Clown Slams throughout Philly and we are excited to bring the Slam to Fringe!
The Philly Clown Slam is an ever-evolving beast of an event - a vehicle (clown car?) for clowns of any kind to come and experiment, and the cast of characters is rotating! We like it this way.

events.title: The Suppliants
events.venue: Asian Arts Initiative Third Floor
events.description:
Inspired by Aeschylus' "The Suppliants" - one of the oldest surviving plays in the Western canon - this new ensemble-driven performance reimagines an ancient story through the lens of Appalachian folklore.
What begins as a tale from the distant past slowly unfolds into something far more immediate: a meditation on refuge, belonging, and the choices communities make when confronted with outsiders seeking safety.
Blending elements of Greek tragedy, folk traditions, movement, and devised performance, the work explores how stories travel across generations and why certain myths refuse to disappear.

events.title: Let Freedom Ring
events.venue: Cherry Street Pier, 121 N Christopher Columbus Blvd, Philadelphia, PA 19106
events.description:
Paul Ramírez Jonas’ monumental artwork plays the song “My Country ‘Tis of Thee” in its entirety—all but the final note. Participants must pull a lever to ring the last note on a 600-pound bell at the base of the sculpture to complete the song, a metaphor for how we can work together as a society to fulfill the unfinished promises of our nation’s founding. This artwork promotes civic engagement by providing a public site to speak, listen, and learn from one another, and to bring people together to imagine a more inclusive future that embraces the complexities of our past.

events.title: Model Republic: Why the American Founders Loved Ancient Carthage
events.venue: National Constitution Center, 525 Arch Street, Philadelphia, PA 19106
events.description:
The National Constitution Center and the University of Pennsylvania Department of Classical Studies present a conversation with renowned Enlightenment scholar and Stanford University Professor Caroline Winterer on how the American founders drew inspiration from not only classical Greece and Rome, but other civilizations in the ancient world, including Carthage, Rome’s mortal enemy. In celebration of America’s 250th anniversary, the conversation will explore how the founders looked much more broadly in the ancient world for inspiration during the American Revolution and how these ideas have shaped our constitutional democracy. Thomas Donnelly, lead scholar at the National Constitution Center, moderates.
After the program, from 6:30 to 7:30 p.

events.title: Reception | "Miles to Go Before We Sleep" solo exhibition by artist Humaira Abid.
events.venue: Pentimenti
events.description:
"Miles to Go Before We Sleep"
HUMAIRA ABID
SEPTEMBER 8 - OCTOBER 24, 2026
RECEPTION: Thursday, September 10 | 6 – 8 PM.
PENTIMENTI is pleased to present "Miles to Go Before We Sleep," a solo exhibition of new wood sculptures and paintings by artist Humaira Abid.
Adapted from Robert Frost's line "And miles to go before I sleep," the title shifts "I" to “we”, turning a personal journey into a collective one. Amid war, displacement, inequality, and ongoing struggles for human rights, the work of repair remains unfinished.
At the core of Abid’s practice are women and the tension between the visible and invisible expectations placed upon them: to nurture, prevail, evolve, and heal, all while navigating restrictions imposed by society or religion.

events.title: Kramer / Fauci
events.venue: FringeArts, 140 N Christopher Columbus Blvd, Philadelphia, PA 19106
events.description:
“God, I hated him.” —Larry Kramer on Anthony Fauci, 2002
“It turned out I loved the guy, and I think he loved me back.” —Anthony Fauci on Larry Kramer, 2020
Internationally acclaimed director Daniel Fish (Oklahoma!) turns his eye to one of the most combustible conversations of the AIDS crisis: the 1993 televised clash between Dr. Anthony Fauci, the nation’s leading AIDS researcher, and playwright-activist Larry Kramer. A confrontation charged with rage, urgency, and unexpected intimacy, it crystallized a turning point in the fight for care, treatment, and recognition. Fish dramatizes their exchange as both history and provocation, a searing reminder of how art, activism, and public health collide on the most human terms.

Welcome to Chekhov’s Banana Peel, the debut production from 21st Century Commedia. This high-octane, relentlessly physical production takes the complete works of Anton Chekhov, the undisputed master of existential subtext and melancholy drama and strips away the subtext entirely. Armed with nothing but physical theatre, high-energy clowning, precision mime, and a healthy dose of theatrical anarchy, our ensemble attempts the impossible: a breakneck, abridged marathon of Chekhov's greatest plays.

One of the most celebrated literary voices of her generation comes to Philadelphia. New York Times bestselling author R.F. Kuang — whose works include The Poppy War trilogy, Babel, and Yellowface — makes a special live appearance in honor of her most anticipated novel yet.
With Taipei Story, Kuang ventures somewhere new: inward. The novel follows Lily, a young women suspended between cultures, who travels to Taiwan searching for the sense of belonging she's never quite found at home. What she uncovers instead is a reckoning — with language, inheritance, and the stories we inherit from those who came before us. Intimate, searching, and emotionally precise, Taipei Story marks a bold new chapter in Kuang's already remarkable career.

Step back and confront the reality of Philadelphia's most devastating epidemic on our Yellow Fever Tour at Christ Church Burial Ground. In late summer 1793, a terrifying fever swept through the nation's capital, taking thousands of lives and sending panic through the streets.
This guide-led tour leads you through the grounds where both victims and key figures of the outbreak. As you walk among the headstones, you will explore 18th-century medical theories, the breakdown of civic life, and the remarkable stories of care and courage that emerged during a citywide crisis.

events.description:
In 1835, PT Barnum exhibited an enslaved woman named Joice Heth as a living curiosity — charging admission to see her, then charging again when she died to watch her public autopsy. Her exploitation launched his career. American circus was born.

It ends gloriously, gorily, and catharically, with Heth getting what she is owed.

The Sicilian Dilemma is play about Identity. a dumbass stoner named me.

events.description:
This world premiere dance-theater piece uses cinematic style to explore familial bonds, love, and heartache.
Mother makes dinner. Daughter sets the table. One empty chair. A knock at the door. Expecting someone? Back to dinner. You made a mistake. Everyone’s watching. The bills pile up. The job’s never done. Another disaster. And your face—it’s older. The cameras are rolling. The Fool is laughing. You’re doing just fine.
Through the eyes of an American family, The Holy Fool examines the toll of aging, grieving, and growing up in a culture where normativity is the most valuable currency. events.title: BLACK D*CK MATTERS by Kathya Alexander
events.venue: IPaM
events.description:
BLACK D*CK MATTER* is a bold, unapologetic new work by acclaimed Seattle playwright Kathya Alexander, directed by Tyrone Brown / Nxt Thrsdy, and presented by The BTMR Project at IPAM as part of the Philadelphia Fringe Festival.
This ensemble-driven production confronts Black masculinity through raw, lyrical storytelling, movement, and monologue. It centers the lived experiences of Black men navigating identity, intimacy, vulnerability, and survival within systems shaped by racism, incarceration, and cultural expectation.
Rather than offering a single narrative, the work builds a series of intersecting portraits—revealing how Black men are seen, judged, and constrained, while also holding space for humor, tenderness, desire, and resilience. I

events.title: The Melon’s Cry

events.description: Set in an NYC private school on the eve of 9/11, The Melon's Cry is a retelling of the poem Goblin Market by Christina Rossetti. Two best friends cling to each other as they are sucked into the inexorable tragedy of sexual maturity and into the void of a post-ideological era. A fable of surrender—willing and unwilling.

events.venue: Asian Arts Initiative Found Spaces
events.description: Do it for me is a wet, one-person performance that explodes ideas of gender and domestic labor through the act of washing laundry, crawling around, cursing dry people, and throwing wet clothes into the air. This is what happens when doing laundry is too much and the performer is mad.

events.description:
Dancing in Yesterday’s Stage Makeup is a kaleidoscopic frolic through the inner worlds of ballet dancers swept up in the excitement of a house party. Joyful chaos blurs the lines between dancers’ realities, revealing glimpses into personal fantasies and emotions. Choreographed sequences mix classical and contemporary ballet lineages with abandon.

events.title: Reckless Abandonment
events.venue: First Unitarian Church of Philadelphia
events.description:
“Reckless Abandonment” explores the concept of “abandon” in all senses of the word. Delving into our body’s living memories of abandon, abandoning, abandonment, and being unbound—we acknowledge the duality that freedom and joy can co-exist with grief, pain, and loss inside our bodies. We explore what it means to move with abandon, without actually abandoning ourselves.
In our culture the word “abandon” has both negative and positive connotations. Having abandonment issues is generally viewed as negative, whereas moving with abandon is something we aspire to. We yearn for this feeling. This dance-theatre work explores both connotations of the word “abandon”, and the explores the relationships between them.
What is the physicality of “leaving”

events.title: Declaration
events.venue: Bob & Selma Horan Studio at the Arden Theatre
events.description:
Reckoning with a life of ambition, compromise and service, a former public official uses the Declaration of Independence to interrogate his life — and ours. As the identities that once defined him are stripped away, he discovers the Declaration anew, forcing him to confront what it still demands of him and us.

events.title: To Root, To Rise
events.venue: Prism Arts Philadelphia, 1021 Hamilton Street, FL 2, Philadelphia, PA 19123
events.description:
To Root, To Rise is an experimental dance duet about the experience of diaspora — about what it means to leave a country and discover that you have brought it with you, imperfectly preserved, inside your muscles and your memory. About the unlived self, the frozen homeland, and the slow construction of a person who is no longer from one place and not yet entirely from another.
Two dancers bring two philosophies of belonging onto the same stage: the tree, whose freedom is earned downward through decades of commitment to one patch of earth; and the bird, whose freedom is the labor of constant negotiation with departure. They are not opposites. They are the same question, asked at different speeds.

events.title: Bride To Be
events.venue: Plays and Players Skinner Studio
events.description:
Bride To Be is a sharp, character-driven comedy about a woman deep in wedding planning. As she juggles cakes, DJs, and mounting family expectations, she begins unraveling the history and cultural weight of marriage — forcing herself to confront what commitment actually means to her. Torn between spectacle and substance, she must decide whether she’s planning a wedding... or redefining it altogether.
Playful, poetic, and sharply relevant, Bride To Be offers a fresh feminist take on saying “I do."
Critics are saying:
"Bride To Be is craft in its highest form. Her energy and storytelling is unmatchable." - Theater Beyond Broadway
"Millane's joy is so overwhelming that the audience can't help getting swept up in it." - Says Me Says Mom

events.title: When Tides Collide
events.venue: Allens Lane Art Center, 601 W Allens Lane, Philadelphia, PA 19119
events.description:
The Shadow Company is a teen-led devised theatre organization of participants aged 13-17 partnered with professional theatre artists. Each year, the Shadow Company devises an original show each year from scratch, through workshops, movement exploration, writing sessions and more.
This year's production is set in a postapocalyptic near future and revolves around themes of groupthink, the ethics of survival, collective memory and collective identity. From the writers: "Being divided as a world has led to neglect of the environment leading to this destruction/disaster. People who have never before thought they could become united have to help each other out in this hard time...leading to complex relationships."

events.title: Agos Y Viento
events.venue: Icebox Project Space Gallery
events.description:
Agos y Viento is a multidisciplinary contemporary opera weaving together Filipino and Latino migratory stories from pre-colonial times to the present, centering on an intergenerational and cross-cultural family. Through poetic verse, video art, devised theater, and dance, the project explores layered histories and identities within one family. We portray how water currents (agos in Tagalog) and wind (viento in Spanish) hold and carry our shared stories across cultural borders and seas, prompting us to question: Where is home?
The AniMalayaWorks Collective draws on the shared tradition of "sarsuela/sarswela"—an opera-style theater form found in both Filipino and Latino cultures—as both a storytelling device and a lens for exploring resistance

events.title: Blue Lightning Ghost Train: Inpatient Program 1
events.venue: Asian Arts Initiative Project Space
events.description: Blue Lightning Ghost Train: Inpatient Program 1 is the first phase of an experimental song, video, and performance cycle using archival materials to explore queer responses to the ongoing opioid crisis. Toying with the notion of performance as harm reduction, the development of the Blue Lightning Ghost Train series has received support from New York State Council on the Arts (NYSCA), a CUNY Social Practice Fellowship, and a Foundation for Contemporary Arts (FCA) Emergency Grant, and features mix engineering by Bassel Al-Rahim and costume design by Connor Goerk.

events.venue: Sidewalk Outside 480 S. Broad St.
events.description:
Celebrate America’s 250th Anniversary with Bodhi’s Guide to History, a new play. In this original work, Bodhi leads a walking tour of Center City and gives his unique – and wildly inaccurate – take on American history. Bodhi is proud to do his own research, but tends to veer hilariously off track; but don't worry, the audience will wind up where the play/tour started.
Bodhi’s Guide to History is the creation of playwright Jim Hawkins, who studied theatre at Villanova University.

events.title: Avalanche of ‘No’
events.venue: Icebox Project Space Gallery
events.description: Combining Shakespeare's language with events from Cousar’s picaresque life, with its absurd calamities and unexpected glories, Avalanche of No will interweave DJ culture, the life of a real-life porter, custody battles, physicalized images of Jean-Michel Basquiat, and 3-card monte into a frank display of bravura storytelling. It will lead audiences into a confrontation of dream with reality, of destiny with real-world circumstance, all filtered through a lens of Afropessimism - experienced by many, recognizable by all. Finally, Cousar plays some of Macbeth, enough to reflect on the Scottish King as a brother of sorts, victim to the fickle mechanisms of destiny.”

events.title: Echoes of Dammām
events.venue: Box Spring Gallery
events.description: Echoes of Dammām is a multimedia storytelling performance that follows fragmented stories gathered around dammām, a ritual drumming practice from Bushehr, a port city in southern Iran. On stage, live narration moves alongside projected video, field recordings, and layered sound. Drums, voices, images, silence, and memory appear in fragments, tracing how grief, resistance, and the struggle for freedom can live inside sonic and bodily practices. Drawing from ethnographic fieldwork in Bushehr, the performance does not tell a single linear story. Instead, it creates an intimate audiovisual space where ritual mourning, Black musical heritage, histories of circulation and loss, and personal memory echo through one another. events.title: Volta
events.venue: SideQuest Theater
events.description:
When Wren arrives at the Mariposa Hotel, she is certain something bad has happened, and she will fix it by finding her sister Lottie. Yet nothing at the Mariposa Hotel moves or functions in quite the way Wren expects. Staff pops out of walls, doors lead to museums where memories stand like sculptures, people call loved ones from other dimensions, and she keeps just missing Lottie. And throughout, a writhing, pulsing, shifting mass invites her to join blissful oblivion. As Wren searches for Lottie, she revisits her life in fits and bursts, finding tenderness, bitterness, loss, and celebration in equal measure.
VOLTA is a play about love's lasting power after the death of the self.
Featuring:
William Acker
Aiden Ankli
Tenara Calem
Arantxa Chav

She’s the eyes of the street – all knowing, all seeing. Don’t dare get on her bad side.
Taking stock of the world on her block in South Philly, Dolores Finnegan tells it like it is and takes no prisoners. Yep, she’s the STOOP BITCH, native to many a neighborhood block and a downright Philly institution. You seen her, you fear her, you trust her – and face it, you know she’s right.
But, what don’t you know? There are ghosts from her past, unfulfilled dreams, battles to be won, and much more to her than meets the eye.
World Premiere –
Written by Daniel Neer
Directed by Ted Gorodetzky
Performed by Lois Sach*.
(*appearing courtesy AEA)
Runtime: 60 minutes with no intermission.

events.title: Enough!
events.venue: Higher Grounds
events.description: Please join Sonja & Stephanie in attempting to determine exactly What is Enough! Can one ever truly know? Maybe Sonja & Stephanie already do know and can help you on your journey to Enough!

events.title: Freedom For A Night
events.venue: Circus Campus
events.description:
Freedom for a Night is a fun, female-empowering circus stage play featuring aerial, spoken word, song, and dance. The iconic "dangerous" women of Greek mythology take center stage to reclaim their stories, rewrite their myths, and challenge the systems that silenced them.
The show comes to the Philadelphia Fringe Festival after a successful Off-Off Broadway production featuring New York City's finest circus artists, the show is written by Caytha Jentis and directed/choreographed by Maia Ramnath.

events.title: Prometheus Bound
events.venue: Yellow Bicycle Theater
events.description: In a race to defeat a cataclysmic computer virus, a psychologist interrogates a quarantined AGI built by his estranged father. A groundbreaking indie film merging live performances with AI-generated worlds. Staged reading, sizzle reel, and audience talkback: a first look for sci-fi fans and backers.

events.title: Enough!
events.venue: Material Culture
events.description: Please join PHFish & Chirps & PHFriends in attempting to determine exactly What is Enough? Can one ever truly know? Maybe PHFish & Chirps & PHFriends (including Greg Goldstein, Meg Sarachan, & Dominic Cardea) already do and can help you on your journey to Enough"

events.title: The Deer Ones
events.venue: Asian Arts Initiative Third Floor
events.description: A multi-media, interactive exploration of childhood memories. The audience is invited to participate as the imaginary friends of a young girl playing in the woods, helping her navigate a series of moral dilemmas. With an ending shaped by audience choice, The Deer Ones asks what does it really mean to care for another, how do we carry (or release) guilt and loss, and how do the ghosts of the past shape the adults of the future.

events.title: The Groundhog
events.venue: Asian Arts Initiative Black Box Theater
events.description:
The Professor gives an excruciatingly detailed lecture on 1993's Groundhog Day while slowly losing control of the classroom, losing the thread of what they meant to say, and losing their grip on reality. A tour de force monologue for one talking clown (like Groucho) and one silent clown (like Harpo). Content warning: Academia, arts education, missing dongles, PowerPoint, teaching the worst class of your life.
A new play by Savannah Reich (Oedipus in Seattle, What is the Butt Game), directed by Francesca Montanile Lyons (Vile, Clowncuterie). Starring Hannah Gold as The Professor and Alex Braslavsky as Sam the TA.

events.title: The Elephant Man
events.venue: Philadelphia Film Society
events.description:
DAVID LYNCH | USA, UK | 1980 | 123 MIN | PG | ENGLISH, FRENCH | 4K
David Lynch’s magnificent follow-up to ERASERHEAD is an atmospheric and touching story about a London surgeon (Anthony Hopkins) discovering the complexity and beauty behind the shocking exterior of an ostracized circus performer (John Hurt).
Cast: Anthony Hopkins, John Hurt, Anne Bancroft
Part of the Philadelphia Film Society’s FILM ESSENTIALS series.
With Film Essentials at the Film Society Center, PFS is giving audiences the chance to experience some of cinema’s greatest treasures as they were meant to be seen: on the big screen!

events.title: Murder at the Netherfield Ball: An Interactive Mytery
events.venue: Elfreth’s Alley Museum, 126 Elfreth's Alley, Philadelphia, PA 19106
events.description:
When someone is murdered at the much anticipated Netherfield Ball, Elizabeth Bennet must clear her family name. But what happens when the loathsome and irritatingly handsome Mr Darcy is the only one who can help her solve the mystery? Join us and the beloved characters of Jane Austen’s Pride and Prejudice outdoors at Elfreth’s Alley for an original interactive murder mystery YOU CAN solve!
Show is approximately 2hrs long. Regency costumes (in the style of Jane Austen and/or Bridgerton, etc) are encouraged but not required!
**Most of the performance will require the audience to move around the space and interact with the characters.**

events.title: The Enemy at Hand
events.venue: Asian Arts Initiative Project Space
events.description:
Between 30 June and 2 July 1934, multiple high ranking Nazi party members were purged on the false suspicion of plotting a coup. Ernst Röhm and members of the Sturmabteilung were apprehended in a surprise attack on the Hanselbauer Hotel in Bad Wiessee. This event originally codenamed "Operation Hummingbird" is commonly referred to as The Night of the Long Knives. Röhm was not the only homosexual Nazi purged, Hitler’s chauffeur later reported that when he and Hitler entered the hotel, an 18 year old paramilitary was found in bed with a leader of the Breslau SA.
The Enemy at Hand, a 50 minute solo show, is about the things people are driven to when their understandings of themselves are warped and clouded. A blackmail web unraveling from 1925

events.title: soft spot
events.venue: Icebox Project Space Gallery
events.description: "soft spot" is a dance work for the child within us, uninhibited and open to the potential of everything. Vyette Tiya and her collaborators use the language of movement to explore tenderness, vulnerability, and intimacy — a glance that turns into a grasp, a tease that turns into a collision, a game that tumbles into freefall. Framed through a series of vignettes, "soft spot" asks: how do we wish to be seen? Who can see us? How do we remain tender in a world that hardens us?

events.title: Free Admission at American Swedish Historical Museum
events.venue: FDR Park, 1500 PATTISON AVENUE, Philadelphia, PA 19145
events.description: The Museum is FREE every second Sunday of the Month.

events.title: Latino Market & Soccer League
events.venue: FDR Park, 1500 PATTISON AVENUE, Philadelphia, PA 19145
events.description: An outdoor market showcasing Latin American flavors, art, and culture!

events.title: Southeast Asian Market
events.venue: FDR Park, 1500 PATTISON AVENUE, Philadelphia, PA 19145
events.description:
Hello. ChomReap Sur. Sabaidee. Sawatdee. Xin Chào. Salam.
The Southeast Asian Market in FDR Park is a community of refugees and immigrant members who have called the Franklin Delano Roosevelt (FDR) Park their home since the 1980’s. For 35+ years they have cultivated an open community space all their own. Here you can enjoy many native cuisine dishes, culturally specific produce, plants, clothing and jewelry, as well as services provided by entrepreneurs speaking multiple languages.

events.title: The Melon’s Cry
events.venue: Rutabaga at the Falls Center
events.description: Set in an NYC private school on the eve of 9/11, The Melon's Cry is a retelling of the poem Goblin Market by Christina Rossetti. Two best friends cling to each other as they are sucked into the inexorable tragedy of sexual maturity and into the void of a post-ideological era. A fable of surrender—willing and unwilling.

events.title: Kachonk
events.venue: Pig Iron Theatre Company
events.description: KACHONK moves loudly through the mundane grind of life, searching for tactile experience and more caffeine. Will they find their purpose? Will they blow out your ear drums? Come scream along with KACHONK in this new evening length performance from Suz Murray. Audiences have called the show "RELATABLE!" and "VERY LOUD!"

events.title: Xposure Rd
events.venue: Hall Pass
events.description: Set in a queer night club, Xposure Rd follows five queer sex workers and their relationships with sexual performance. When the owner of the club threatens to censor the performers, they start to rebel against him. Paulie and Maxxx are at a crossroads: do they want to continue performing? As they struggle with planning for their future, they celebrate the community they’ve formed. With the use of musical interludes inspired by burlesque, porn, and private dancing, Xposure Rd take you on an intimate drive through the sex work industry. What are the limits to sexual performance? And can we take you over the edge? Content Warning: This piece contains full nudity, stimulated masturbation, and mentions of abortion. Xposure Rd was originally writte

events.title: Masks Off
events.venue: Roxborough Pocket Park
events.description: "Masks Off" is an exploration of identity through dance and music. El Rizal flows and moves with costuming and movement informed by their Indonesian heritage. Joshua Marquez pounds Filipino percussion over broken beats in this collaborative attempt to shed masks and find diasporic identity.

events.title: Bodhi’s Guide to History
events.venue: Sidewalk Outside 480 S. Broad St.
events.description:
Celebrate America’s 250th Anniversary with Bodhi’s Guide to History, a new play. In this original work, Bodhi leads a walking tour of Center City and gives his unique – and wildly inaccurate – take on American history. Bodhi is proud to do his own research, but tends to veer hilariously off track; but don't worry, the audience will wind up where the play/tour started.
Bodhi’s Guide to History is the creation of playwright Jim Hawkins, who studied theatre at Villanova University.

events.title: Jade Chloe
events.venue: Performance Garage
events.description:
Jade Chloe is a showcase encompassing Jade’s life for the past year and the soundtrack that best speaks that period . This showcase is an expression of a distinct beginning and end to the experiences of a particular time. A singular story is told through several phrases of movement by a cast of talented dancers.
As Jade Chloe has trained under the Alvin Ailey American Dance Theatre, the Steps on Broadway Academy, and now Philadelphia ballet, her choreography is inspired by a plethora of styles and techniques. However the show can be classified as a contemporary dance performance with heavy jazz and modern influences.
Get your tickets to see an emerging artist in motion

events.title: Moral Injury
events.venue: First Unitarian Church of Philadelphia
events.description: Dil and Dak are stranded on a deserted island. Desperate and starving, the two attempt to hunt and consume a pig, with dire consequences. Chaos ensues in this genre-blending performance piece featuring heavy movement, mask, and sound work

events.title: Wikipedilove
events.venue: Studio 34, 4522 Baltimore Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19143
events.description:
Original musical comedy based on Wikipedia articles about love and sex with humans and other tragic animals. Using a projector to show articles, photos, and videos, listen and laugh to songs about topics including the brief romantic life moths, kinky and consent focused whales, Hitler's tragic love life, and the town of Dildo, Canada.
 - Edmonton Journal
 “Laughed the entire hour of this hilarious show” - Alberta Prime Times
